DW.app.title: Downtime Work
DW.button.label: Downtime
DW.hint.character: Decides whose journal this is filed under and who speaks the chat card, and supplies the character's level. Every other rule input is entered by hand.
DW.hint.classLevel: Sets the monthly XP threshold (p. 423). It only matters for activities that earn campaign XP.
DW.hint.castings: Enter how many spells of each level the character can cast in a day. The market cap is 9 − (market class + spell level), and one casting in six sells (p. 172).
DW.hint.perpetual: An upfront fee plus a monthly maintenance fee, because a caster can only sustain so many perpetual effects at once (p. 173).
DW.hint.specialist: The wage an employer would pay is what the character earns by hiring himself out. Quantity is months, days or pages, whichever the grade is priced in (pp. 170–172).
DW.hint.trade: The character's own output plus every subordinate's, each raised by half again for being supervised. Subordinates beyond what the rank permits are not counted.
DW.hint.labor: A flat 6gp per month. Labor is the one trade that does not improve with further ranks (p. 113).
DW.hint.gambling: 1d6 exploding per rank per week of dedicated activity, averaging 4.2gp a die (p. 111).
DW.hint.market: Market impact is cargo capacity divided by the market's baseline, rounded — 30,000 st in a Class I market, 150 st in a village. It is capped at 10 outside a Class I market, and a caravan too small for a market trades it as a smaller one instead (p. 371).
DW.hint.merchandise: The demand modifier is the Judge's, one per merchandise per market: low where the market produces it, high where it must import it. Assess supply and demand to learn it (p. 373).
DW.hint.price: The price moves in steps of its own size. The 4d4−10 is thrown once per merchandise per market per month; the negotiation is worth one more step, in your favour whichever way you are trading (pp. 375–376).
DW.hint.deal: How much you actually want to move today. Anything beyond what the market will bear is not priced.
DW.hint.ledger: The month for the venture as a whole, revenue above and costs below (p. 423). The purchase price of merchandise you have not sold yet is not a cost — it counts in the month you sell it.
DW.hint.participants: Half the profit goes to the owners of the venture's assets, pro rata, and half to the people who ran it — henchmen and followers at a half share each. Ownership can be percentages or the gold each put in; either works.
DW.hint.overrides: Leave blank to use the figure the rules produce, shown greyed in the box. Anything you type replaces it.
DW.tip.character: Whose downtime journal this record is filed under, who speaks the chat card, and where the level box is filled from. Nothing else is read off the sheet.
DW.tip.recordName: The name of the journal page this is saved as. Left blank, the activity's own name is used.
DW.tip.classLevel: Drives the monthly XP threshold (p. 423): campaign income earns XP only above it. Irrelevant to wage work, which earns no XP at all.
DW.tip.activity: Which downtime work the character is doing. The inputs and the rulebook page below both follow from it.
DW.tip.magicType: Arcane or divine. It does not change the fee, which is the same for both, only how many rival casters the market holds (p. 172).
DW.tip.marketClass: Class I is a metropolis, Class VI a village. It caps how many castings of each level will sell in a day: 9 − (class + level).
DW.tip.daysWorked: Days spent selling spells as a dedicated activity. Thirty is a full month.
DW.tip.castings: How many spells of this level the character can cast per day. Whatever exceeds the market cap simply does not sell.
DW.tip.perpetualLevel: The level of the perpetual spell being sustained. Higher levels cost far more, both upfront and monthly (p. 173).
DW.tip.perpetualCount: How many effects of this level are being sustained for the client.
DW.tip.specialist: Which specialist's trade the character is plying. The figure is the wage an employer pays, which is what he earns (pp. 170–172).
DW.tip.grade: The specialist's rank or speciality, which sets the wage and what it is per — a month, a day, or a page.
DW.tip.quantity: How many months, days or pages of work, matching whatever the chosen grade is priced in.
DW.tip.patients: Healers billing by the day charge per patient, so this multiplies the wage (p. 171).
DW.tip.rank: How many times the proficiency has been taken. Each rank raises the monthly figure and how many subordinates may be supervised.
DW.tip.months: Months of dedicated activity. Anything less than a full month scales the income down.
DW.tip.workers: Subordinates of this rank under supervision. Each earns their own rank's figure raised by half again. More than the rank permits are not counted.
DW.tip.ranks: Ranks of the Gambling proficiency. Each rank adds one exploding d6 per week (p. 111).
DW.tip.weeks: Weeks of dedicated activity at the tables. Gambling is paid by the week, not the month.
DW.tip.overrideGold: Replaces the derived income outright. The rules' own figure is shown greyed in the box and kept in the record.
DW.tip.manualTotal: Rolling physical dice? Type the total here and it is used instead — no dice animation fires, and the card says the result was entered rather than rolled.
DW.tip.arbMarketClass: The market being traded in. It sets the baseline cargo that market impact is measured against, the toll, and how much of each merchandise changes hands in a day.
DW.tip.cargoCapacity: What the whole caravan or fleet can carry, in stone — not what it is carrying. Both market impact and the toll are worked out from capacity.
DW.tip.urbanFamilies: Only a Class I market scales past an impact of 10, and then by its families divided by 2,000.
DW.tip.partySize: How many characters are entering the market separately. Each of them is then capped at 10 divided by that number; leave it at 1 for entering alone or as one party.
DW.tip.mercantileNetwork: Having traded here before is worth either one market class or one point of impact, whichever moves more goods. It never raises the toll.
DW.tip.rulersPrivilege: A character trading in a domain he rules pays no toll, tariff, moorage or stabling.
DW.tip.merchandise: Which of the 29 types of merchandise is being traded today. Each has its own base price, its own price step, and its own daily volume by market class.
DW.tip.side: Buying moves the price down when it moves in your favour; selling moves it up. It also decides whether a tariff is owed.
DW.tip.demandModifier: The Judge's figure for this merchandise in this market: negative where it is produced and cheap, positive where it must be imported and dear. Each point is one price step.
DW.tip.season: Grain and vegetables cost a step more while they are being sown and a step less at harvest. Nothing else moves with the season.
DW.tip.steadyRoute: An established route in this merchandise adds half the character's class level to market impact, and one price step in his favour.
DW.tip.exhaustionSteps: The optional rule for working a market dry: each step moves the price against you — up if you are buying, down if you are selling.
DW.tip.priceRoll: 4d4−10, thrown once per merchandise per market per month, so −6 to +6 steps. Roll it with the die button or type what was rolled at the table.
DW.tip.negotiation: The outcome of haggling. Agreement and grudging agreement each move the price one step in your favour; a refusal ends it, and an outraged one locks you out of that merchandise for the month.
DW.tip.assessment: A day spent learning the market's demand modifiers. It reveals prices rather than changing them, so it does not enter the arithmetic.
DW.tip.chaMod: The character's Charisma modifier, added to both the assessment and the negotiation roll.
DW.tip.wilMod: The character's Will modifier. It replaces Charisma once a negotiation has become a contest of wills.
DW.tip.bargainingRanks: Each rank of Bargaining is worth +2 to the negotiation roll, and each of the merchant's is worth −2.
DW.tip.merchantExtraRank: The Judge secretly rolls 1d6 when bargaining opens; over the market's class, the merchant has one more rank of Bargaining than usual.
DW.tip.stone: How much to buy or sell today. The market takes only what it will bear, however much is offered.
DW.tip.ledgerRevenue: Gold the venture took in this month, from selling cargo, carrying freight and carrying passengers.
DW.tip.ledgerCostOfGoods: What the merchandise sold this month cost. Goods still in the hold are not counted until they are sold — and treasure sold into the market costs its base price, which was already claimed as adventuring XP.
DW.tip.ledgerExpense: A cost the venture carried this month. The book's list is wages, rations, tolls, tariffs, moorage and stabling, and labor fees.
DW.tip.capital: What was put into the venture — the ships, the wagons and the working funds. It decides the rate of return, not the income or the XP.
DW.tip.participantName: Whatever this person is called at the table. It is only a label; the record is filed under the character chosen at the top.
DW.tip.participantRole: A player character takes a full operator's share, a henchman or follower half a share, and a hired mercenary or specialist none at all.
DW.tip.participantOwnership: This person's stake in the venture's assets. Percentages or the gold each contributed both work — the split is pro rata either way.
DW.tip.participantLevel: This person's own class level, which sets their own monthly XP threshold. A share below it earns no XP.
DW.activityHint.spellcasting: A day spent selling spells in a market. One casting in six sells, and no market absorbs more than 9 − (class + level) of a given level per day.
DW.activityHint.perpetualSpellcasting: Sustaining perpetual effects for a client: a fee upfront, and a smaller one every month it lasts.
DW.activityHint.specialist: Hiring out at the wage the specialist tables list. A master-rank proficiency is what qualifies a character to do this.
DW.activityHint.artCraft: Making goods to sell, alone or with a workshop of subordinates under supervision.
DW.activityHint.profession: Practising a civil profession — actuary, banker, lawyer, scribe, seneschal and the like.
DW.activityHint.performance: Acting, dancing, singing, reciting or playing for fees, alone or leading a troupe.
DW.activityHint.labor: Honest manual work. It pays badly and never pays better, but it never runs out either.
DW.activityHint.gambling: Games of chance and skill, by the week. The dice explode, so a good week can be very good.
DW.activityHint.arbitrage: A day in one market, in one merchandise: what it costs there, how much of it the market will take, and what the haggling did to the price.
DW.activityHint.mercantileVenture: The month totalled for the venture as a whole, and the profit divided between the people who own it and the people who ran it. This is where mercantile XP is earned.
DW.results.noXp: None. Wages and fees earn no campaign XP (p. 423).
DW.results.xpAgainstThreshold: Income above the monthly threshold of {threshold}gp (p. 423).
DW.results.overrideTooltip: The figure the rules produced, replaced by the Judge.
DW.results.expected: Expected income; nothing has been rolled yet.
DW.results.dealValue: The value of one day's trade at the market price shown.
DW.results.monthTotal: The venture's month, revenue less costs.
DW.results.noXpArbitrage: None from a single day's trade. Mercantile income is the venture's whole month, net of goods and costs (p. 424).
DW.results.entryCostNote: paid on entering the market, not on this deal
DW.results.unsoldNotCounted: Merchandise bought but not yet sold is not a cost this month — it counts against the month it sells in (p. 424).
DW.warn.marketWillNotAbsorb: A {market} takes at most {cap} castings of level {level} a day; {offered} were offered.
DW.warn.marketTooSmall: A {market} will not take a single casting of any level offered.
DW.warn.workersOverLimit: {employed} subordinates of this rank, but only {allowed} may be supervised. The rest are not counted.
DW.warn.noRank: At rank 0 the character has no such proficiency and earns nothing.
DW.warn.noDaysWorked: No days worked, so nothing is earned.
DW.warn.noMonthsWorked: No months worked, so nothing is earned.
DW.warn.noWeeksWorked: No weeks worked, so nothing is earned.
DW.warn.noQuantity: No months, days or pages of work entered.
DW.warn.merchandiseUnavailable: No {merchandise} is traded in a market this small at this demand.
DW.warn.belowOneStone: Only {available} stone a day is available, and less than a stone cannot be traded. It takes {days} days of soliciting to accumulate one.
DW.warn.quantityCapped: {requested} stone offered, but the market will only take {available}. The rest is not priced.
DW.warn.noStone: No stone entered, so nothing changes hands.
DW.warn.priceFloored: {steps} price steps would take the price to nothing or below. It is held at one step instead — the rules print no floor, so the Judge should set one.
DW.warn.ventureAtALoss: The venture lost {income}gp this month. Only a profit is divided, so nobody earns campaign XP.
DW.warn.noParticipants: Nobody is listed as sharing in the venture, so the profit is not divided.
DW.warn.noSelfParticipant: No participant is marked as this character, so the panel above shows no share.
DW.warn.noOwnership: Nobody is recorded as owning any of the venture's assets, so half the profit is left undivided.
DW.warn.hirelingHasNoShare: {name} is a hireling: hired mercenaries and specialists get no share of profit, so the ownership entered is not counted.
DW.action.reopen: Reopen in the Downtime Work wizard
DW.note.impactCapped: Market impact {from} is more than this market can service; it is capped at {to}.
DW.note.impactShared: Entering separately as {partySize} caps each of them at market impact {to}.
DW.note.impactSteppedDown: Too small to register here, so the market is traded as a {market} instead. Tolls are unaffected.
DW.note.villageFloor: A village can always be traded in at market impact 1.
DW.note.networkRescued: Having traded here before is worth market impact 1 on its own.
DW.note.networkClass: Having traded here before, the market is treated as a {market}. Tolls are unaffected.
DW.note.networkImpact: Having traded here before raises market impact to {to}. Tolls are unaffected.
DW.note.steadyRoute: A steady trade route adds {bonus} to market impact.
DW.note.steadyRouteClass: That exceeds what this market will bear, so it advances to a {market}.
DW.notify.saveFailed: Could not save the downtime record. See the console for details.
DW.notify.recordNotFound: That downtime record could not be found. Its journal page may have been deleted.
DW.notify.recordTooOld: That record was saved before the wizard stored its inputs, so it can be read but not reopened.
DW.notify.nothingToRoll: This activity is not decided by dice; its income is fixed.
DW.dialog.duplicate.title: Record already exists
DW.dialog.duplicate.content: "{name}" is already a page in {journal}. Replace it?
DW.journal.title: {name} - {label}
DW.setting.journalLabel.name: Downtime journal name
DW.setting.journalLabel.hint: The label that follows the character's name, so a journal is called "Elaria - Downtime".
DW.setting.buttonVisibility.name: Who sees the Downtime button
DW.setting.buttonVisibility.hint: Whether the Actor Directory button is shown to everyone or only to the GM.
DW.activityHint.hijink: One job, alone or with a crew. Whatever it earns goes to the boss; each perpetrator who gets away keeps half of his own share as XP.
DW.activityHint.syndicate: A criminal guild's month: tribute from the idle, earnings from the busy, less what the lawyers and the bribes cost. This is where a boss earns campaign XP.
DW.results.toEveryThrow: to every throw, for the crew's size
DW.results.xpHalfValue: Half the gp value of what he pulled off. No threshold is subtracted — a member is the one earner in the book measured this way (p. 423).
DW.hint.hijink: Enter what the throws came to: who made it, and who was caught. A throw failed by 14 or more, or an unmodified 1, is an arrest — 11 or a 1–3 if he never lay low after his last job. If anyone is caught, everyone who missed is caught with him.
DW.hint.syndicateMembers: Members given no orders pay tribute instead, and the table is tuned to make that an even trade with ordering them about. Members above the market's effective level pay at the ceiling.
DW.hint.syndicateLedger: Tribute and wages are worked out from the table above, so they have no boxes of their own here. The rest is the book's own list of what a boss pays for: attorneys, bribes, fines and healing (p. 423).
DW.warn.crewOverSlots: The honcho can run {slots} without penalty; every extra perpetrator is −1 on everyone's throw, for −{penalty} in all.
DW.warn.hijinkFailed: Nobody made their throw, so the hijink earned nothing.
DW.warn.perpetratorsCaught: {count} caught. They forfeit their share, and the boss is expected to pay for their lawyers, bribes, fines and healing.
DW.warn.overMaxMembers: {headcount} members, but a syndicate this size needs a bigger hideout or a bigger settlement — the ceiling here is {max}.
DW.warn.ordersExceedMembers: {ordered} orders given to {headcount} members. A boss may only assign one hijink each per month without a loyalty roll.
DW.warn.syndicateAtALoss: The syndicate lost {income}gp this month, so there is no campaign XP in it.
DW.note.hijinkHasNoCashValue: {hijink} has no cash value; it is done to warn, to avenge, or to open the way to something else.
DW.note.effectiveLevelCapped: A {market} reaches only {cap}th level of loot and targets. Throws still use the perpetrator's own level.
DW.note.syndicateCappedByMarket: The hideout would support more, but a {market} sustains only {max} members.
DW.note.hideoutCouldGrow: The hideout supports {byHideout} members; this settlement would sustain {marketCap}.
DW.tip.hijink: Which job is being pulled. It sets the thief skill thrown against, how long each stage takes, and what a success is worth to the boss.
DW.tip.hijinkMarket: Where the job is done. The settlement's class caps the level of loot and of targets available — a village holds nothing worth more than 3rd level.
DW.tip.victimLevel: The victim's own level, which is what the bounty or ransom scales with. A 0th level victim counts as half a level.
DW.tip.hasty: Carousing, racketeering and soliciting can be rushed: far quicker, much less valuable, and a botched throw gets a second chance before an arrest.
DW.tip.crewName: Whatever this perpetrator is called at the table. It is only a label.
DW.tip.crewLevel: This perpetrator's class level. The levels of everyone who succeeds are added together to set what the job was worth, and the loot is split by level among whoever got away.
DW.tip.crewCha: Charisma, which decides how large a crew this perpetrator can run as honcho and breaks a tie for who the honcho is.
DW.tip.crewSucceeded: Did he make his throw? One success is enough for the job to come off, and a perpetrator who succeeded is never caught.
DW.tip.crewCaught: Did he fail by 14 or more, or roll an unmodified 1? If anyone is caught, everyone who missed their throw is caught with him.
DW.tip.syndicateMarket: The settlement the hideout stands within six miles of. It caps both how large the syndicate can grow and the level its members can reach.
DW.tip.hideoutValue: What the hideout is worth. Each tier of value supports a larger syndicate, up to whatever the settlement itself will sustain.
DW.tip.members: How many members of this level the syndicate holds. Any who are given no orders pay tribute instead.
DW.tip.assigned: How many members of this level were ordered out on a job. Each is paid a fee — 6gp at 0th level, a month's henchman wages above it.
DW.tip.hijinkEarnings: What the ordered jobs actually brought in. Work it out on the Perpetrate a hijink activity and enter the total here.
DW.tip.syndicateExpense: A cost the boss carried this month. The book's list is attorneys, bribes, fines and magical healing for members who got caught (p. 423).
DW.label.levelFromActor: Take the level from the character sheet
DW.tip.levelFromActor: Fills the level box from the picked character's sheet, and re-fills it if you pick a different character. Typing over the box clears this, and your number stands until you tick it again. Nothing else is read off the sheet.
DW.notify.rollFailed: The dice could not be rolled. See the console for details.
